slot.brief: Average speed question: a body covers two equal distances at speeds v1 and v2; compare its average speed with the arithmetic mean of the speeds.

stem: An automated cart covers two equal-length sections of a route at speeds of $12$ m s$^{-1}$ and $24$ m s$^{-1}$. Which pair gives its average speed and its comparison with the arithmetic mean of these speeds?
options: $16$ m s$^{-1}$, less than the arithmetic mean
$18$ m s$^{-1}$, equal to the arithmetic mean
$20$ m s$^{-1}$, greater than the arithmetic mean
$24$ m s$^{-1}$, greater than the arithmetic mean

verdicts.working: For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean: $2(12)(24)/(12+24)=16$ m s$^{-1}$. The arithmetic mean is $18$ m s$^{-1}$, so the average speed is less.

working:
$v_{\text{avg}}=\dfrac{2(12)(24)}{12+24}=16$ m s$^{-1}$
$\dfrac{12+24}{2}=18$ m s$^{-1}$
Hence $v_{\text{avg}}<\dfrac{12+24}{2}$.

Independent check: For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean: $2(12)(24)/(12+24)=16$ m s$^{-1}$. The arithmetic mean is $18$ m s$^{-1}$, so the average speed is less.
